question.problem:
Find a $2\times 2$ matrix $A$ that has eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=-3$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=3,$ and corresponding eigenvectors

$$
{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$
question.worked_solution:
Since $B=\{{v}_{1},{v}_{2}\}$ is a basis of ${R}^{2}$ consisting of the eigenvectors of $A$, then  $A$ must be diagonalizable. 

So, we can write $A=PD{P}^{-1},$ where $P$ is a matrix whose columns are the eigenvectors of $A$ and $D$ is a diagonal matrix whose entries are the eigenvalues in the corresponding order:

$$
A={{[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ {v}_{1} & {v}_{2} \\ | & |\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{P}{{[\begin{aligned}{\lambda }_{1} & 0 \\ 0 & {\lambda }_{2}\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{D}{{{[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ {v}_{1} & {v}_{2} \\ | & |\end{aligned}]}^{-1}}_{⏟}}_{{P}^{-1}}
$$

Let $P=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}].$ Then,

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}^{-1} & ={[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}=-\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ -1 & -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, carrying out the necessary matrix multiplication, we obtain,

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-3 & 0 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}](-\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ -1 & -2\end{aligned}]) \\  & =-\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}6 & 3 \\ -3 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ -1 & -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 4 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
